modules.name: Klar
modules.purpose: Klar (Norwegian for "clear" and "ready") is a toolkit of interface components for data-intensive applications.
modules.whenToUse: you start any application with Klar, to put its stylesheet on the page once.
modules.whenNot: you look for a component, each of which has its own module (`Klar.Button`, `Klar.Table`); this module holds only the stylesheet.

modules.name: Klar.Theme
modules.purpose: The look of the application: ten themes, each in a light and a dark mode, and the small shared vocabulary of the components: the color of a message (`Tone`), the size of a control (`Size`) and how ...
modules.whenToUse: the application picks one of the ten themes, or a person picks the mode (light, dark or the system's); or you give a component a tone, a size or a density.
modules.whenNot: you want colors of your own. There is no way to make one on purpose: the themes are drawn so that every pair of colors in the library keeps WCAG AA contrast, which a color picked in a form would not.

modules.name: Klar.Color
modules.purpose: A color that comes from data: the color of a status, a category, a team, a customer.
modules.whenToUse: the color is a value of your data (a `Maybe String` code from a backend, a color in a record) and a component should show it.
modules.whenNot: the color means success, warning or danger; use a `Tone` (`Klar.Theme`), which follows the theme and the dark mode. Do not use it for the look of the application, which is the theme.

modules.name: Klar.Settings
modules.purpose: What the application says once and every component follows: how tightly things are packed (the density), the time zone of the times people read, and the theme and mode (light or dark) of the look.
modules.whenToUse: the application chooses a density or knows the time zone of its users, which is every application with a clock in it.
modules.whenNot: you want colors of your own; the application picks one of the ten themes of `Klar.Theme`, and nothing else.

modules.name: Klar.Locale
modules.purpose: The language and the regional conventions of the text the library writes itself: placeholders such as "Search ...", the labels of icon buttons, month names, validation messages, number separators.
modules.whenToUse: the text the library writes itself must come in another language than English, or you pick between two of your own texts.
modules.whenNot: you need to translate your own labels and messages, which stay in your application.

modules.name: Klar.Layout
modules.purpose: Layout primitives: vertical stacks, horizontal rows and grids, with spacing from a fixed scale.
modules.whenToUse: you arrange content in stacks, rows, grids or a page column with spacing from the design scale.
modules.whenNot: you need a frame for a whole application (as `Klar.AppShell`) or a grouped surface (as `Klar.Card`).

modules.name: Klar.Card
modules.purpose: A bordered surface that groups related content, with an optional header and footer.
modules.whenToUse: related content belongs together on a bordered surface with an optional title, actions and footer.
modules.whenNot: the content is a whole page region with its own header (as `Klar.PageHeader`) or an overlay (as `Klar.Modal`).

modules.name: Klar.Text
modules.purpose: Typography: titles, paragraphs, small print and code.
modules.whenToUse: the page needs titles, paragraphs, small print or code that look the same everywhere.
modules.whenNot: the text is a link (use `Klar.Link`), an action (use `Klar.Button`) or key caps (use `Klar.Kbd`).

modules.name: Klar.Icon
modules.purpose: Line icons.
modules.whenToUse: a button, menu item or message needs a small line icon that follows the text color.
modules.whenNot: you need one of the rarer icons, which live in the `Klar.Icon.*` modules, or a picture (use an `img`).

modules.name: Klar.Button
modules.purpose: Buttons and button-looking links.
modules.whenToUse: the user must trigger an action, or follow a link that should look like a button.
modules.whenNot: you need a plain link in running text (as `Klar.Link`) or a choice between options (as `Klar.SegmentedControl`).

modules.name: Klar.Menu
modules.purpose: A dropdown menu opened from a button.
modules.whenToUse: a few actions do not deserve their own buttons: row actions, "more", user menus.
modules.whenNot: the popup holds any content (as `Klar.Popover`), opens on right-click (as `Klar.ContextMenu`) or has a main action (as `Klar.SplitButton`).

modules.name: Klar.ButtonGroup
modules.purpose: Buttons that belong together, joined into one block: shared borders, only the outer corners rounded, and one focus ring per button that always stays in view.
modules.whenToUse: actions that are close in meaning should read as one joined control, such as "Edit / Duplicate / Print".
modules.whenNot: the user chooses between views (as `Klar.SegmentedControl`), options are on or off (as `Klar.ToggleGroup`) or one action has alternatives (as `Klar.SplitButton`).

modules.name: Klar.ToggleGroup
modules.purpose: A row of toggle buttons for choices that can be on or off: "Bold / Italic / Underline", the statuses to show in a list, the days of the week.
modules.whenToUse: the user turns options on or off in a compact row, such as "Bold / Italic / Underline" or a set of statuses.
modules.whenNot: exactly one view is always chosen (as `Klar.SegmentedControl`) or each choice needs an explanation (as `Klar.CheckboxGroup` or `Klar.Radio`).

modules.name: Klar.SplitButton
modules.purpose: A main action with a few alternatives: a button joined to a small arrow that opens a menu. "Save" with "Save and close" and "Save as draft" behind the arrow.
modules.whenToUse: one main action has a few alternatives behind an arrow, such as "Save" and "Save and close".
modules.whenNot: the actions are equal (as `Klar.ButtonGroup`) or there is no main action (as `Klar.Menu`).

modules.name: Klar.Link
modules.purpose: A real link (`<a href>`) that cannot be built wrong: for a page of the application, for another site, for an email address or a telephone number.
modules.whenToUse: the user navigates to a page of the application, another site, an email address or a phone number.
modules.whenNot: the click is an action and not a navigation (as `Klar.Button`).

modules.name: Klar.Kbd
modules.purpose: Keyboard keys as key caps, for hints and documentation: "Ctrl K", "Shift Enter", or a sequence such as "G then O".
modules.whenToUse: a hint or help text must show a keyboard shortcut as key caps.
modules.whenNot: you need to listen to the shortcut (as `Klar.Shortcut`) or list all shortcuts (as `Klar.ShortcutHelp`).

modules.name: Klar.Badge
modules.purpose: Small read-only labels for state and metadata, such as "Paid" or "Overdue", and round number badges.
modules.whenToUse: the user must read a state or a count, such as "Paid", "Overdue" or a number.
modules.whenNot: the label is something the user picked and can remove (as `Klar.Tag`).

modules.name: Klar.Tag
modules.purpose: A chip: a short label for a value, a filter or a selection, optionally with a remove button.
modules.whenToUse: a chip shows a value, filter or selection that the user chose and can take away.
modules.whenNot: the label is a read-only state (as `Klar.Badge`).

modules.name: Klar.Alert
modules.purpose: Inline messages that tell the user something important in the context where it matters: information, success, a warning or an error.
modules.whenToUse: the user must see an important message in the place where it matters.
modules.whenNot: the message should disappear by itself (as `Klar.Toast`).

modules.name: Klar.Spinner
modules.purpose: Loading indicators: a small spinner for inline use and a centered panel for a region that is still loading.
modules.whenToUse: you do not know what the content will look like or how long the wait will be.
modules.whenNot: you can sketch the content (use `Klar.Skeleton`) or want a bar that shows how far a task has come (use `Klar.Progress`).

modules.name: Klar.Skeleton
modules.purpose: Shimmering placeholders that stand in for content while it loads.
modules.whenToUse: you can sketch what the content will look like (a title, a few lines, a picture) while it loads.
modules.whenNot: you cannot predict the shape of the content (use `Klar.Spinner`).

modules.name: Klar.Progress
modules.purpose: Progress: a linear bar, a bar divided into steps, and a ring.
modules.whenToUse: you can say how far a task has come, as a percentage or as steps such as "3 of 5".
modules.whenNot: there is nothing to measure and a plain wait will do (use `Klar.Spinner`).

modules.name: Klar.EmptyState
modules.purpose: What to show when there is nothing to show: an empty list, no search results, a first-run screen.
modules.whenToUse: a list or a screen of your own is empty and the user should be told why and what to do next.
modules.whenNot: a request failed (use `Klar.ErrorState`).

modules.name: Klar.ErrorState
modules.purpose: What to show when a request failed: a clear title, the reason, and a button to try again when trying again can help.
modules.whenToUse: a request failed and the user should see why, with a button to try again.
modules.whenNot: a list is simply empty (use `Klar.EmptyState`).

modules.name: Klar.Form
modules.purpose: A form as one value: the text and choices of every field, which fields the user has left, what the server refused, the rows of a repeating group, the step the user is on, and whether anything has ...
modules.whenToUse: you edit a record in a form and want the values, rules, steps and server problems kept in one state.
modules.whenNot: the form is hand-wired or only needs a frame (use `Klar.Form.Layout`), or one value saves by itself (use `Klar.InlineEdit`).

modules.name: Klar.Form.Spec
modules.purpose: The declaration of a form: its fields in order, each with a label and its rules, grouped in steps.
modules.whenToUse: you declare the fields, labels, rules and steps of a form once, at the top of the file that owns it.
modules.whenNot: you keep or change form state at run time (use `Klar.Form`).

modules.name: Klar.Form.Layout
modules.purpose: The layout of a form and the parts around it.
modules.whenToUse: you need the frame of a form (sections, grid, button row, status of the save, unsaved mark) or wire a form by hand.
modules.whenNot: you want values, rules, steps and problems kept for you (use `Klar.Form`).

modules.name: Klar.Form.Check
modules.purpose: Tests for a form: what an `elm-test` file needs to be sure that a declaration is right, in one line each.
modules.whenToUse: you write an `elm-test` file for a form declared with `Klar.Form.Spec`.
modules.whenNot: you declare or draw a form (use `Klar.Form.Spec` and `Klar.Form`); this module is for tests only.

modules.name: Klar.Field
modules.purpose: The wrapper around a form control: a label, a required or optional mark, a hint and an error message, joined to the control for screen readers.
modules.whenToUse: you build a custom control that should look and behave like the other fields (label, hint, error).
modules.whenNot: you use a control from this package such as `Klar.TextInput` or `Klar.Select`; they wrap themselves in a field.

modules.name: Klar.Validate
modules.purpose: Pure, composable validators for text values.
modules.whenToUse: you check text values by hand and want messages in the user's language.
modules.whenNot: you declare a form with `Klar.Form.Spec`, which takes the same validators as its rules.

modules.name: Klar.TextInput
modules.purpose: A single-line text input with a label, a hint and an error message.
modules.whenToUse: you need one line of text and want to own the value in your model.
modules.whenNot: the value is a number, a password, a search, tags or several lines (use `Klar.NumberInput`, `Klar.PasswordInput`, `Klar.SearchInput`, `Klar.TagInput` or `Klar.TextArea`).

modules.name: Klar.TextArea
modules.purpose: A multi-line text field with a label, a hint and an error message.
modules.whenToUse: you need text of several lines, such as a note or a description.
modules.whenNot: one line is enough (use `Klar.TextInput`).

modules.name: Klar.NumberInput
modules.purpose: A number field that understands how people write numbers.
modules.whenToUse: the value is a number that people type in their own way, with limits, decimals or a unit.
modules.whenNot: the value is plain text (use `Klar.TextInput`).

modules.name: Klar.PasswordInput
modules.purpose: A password field with a "show password" button and an optional strength meter.
modules.whenToUse: the user types a password and may want to see it, or you want to show its strength.
modules.whenNot: the text is not secret (use `Klar.TextInput`).

modules.name: Klar.SearchInput
modules.purpose: A search field that waits until the user stops typing.
modules.whenToUse: a list is filtered or searched as the user types and you want one message when the typing pauses.
modules.whenNot: you need an ordinary text field (use `Klar.TextInput`) or suggestions to pick from (use `Klar.Autocomplete`).

modules.name: Klar.TagInput
modules.purpose: Free-form tags: type a word, press Enter or comma, get a chip.
modules.whenToUse: the user enters a list of free words, such as keywords or e-mail addresses.
modules.whenNot: the tags come from a fixed list (use `Klar.MultiSelect`).

modules.name: Klar.FileDrop
modules.purpose: Choose files by dropping them on a zone or with a "Choose files" button.
modules.whenToUse: a form where the choice of files matters and the application only needs their names, sizes and types.
modules.whenNot: you want the library to upload or read the file (it hands over the `File`; the request is yours).

modules.name: Klar.InlineEdit
modules.purpose: Click-to-edit text.
modules.whenToUse: a single text that is edited in place and saved at once, such as a customer name on a detail page.
modules.whenNot: the text is one field of a form that is saved with a button; use `Klar.TextInput`.

modules.name: Klar.Checkbox
modules.purpose: A checkbox, with a label or bare.
modules.whenToUse: a yes or no choice that is saved together with the rest of a form, or a bare box in a table row.
modules.whenNot: the setting takes effect at once (`Klar.Switch`) or several related choices share one label (`Klar.CheckboxGroup`).

modules.name: Klar.CheckboxGroup
modules.purpose: A group of checkboxes: choose any number of the options.
modules.whenToUse: a handful of options where the user may choose any number and should see them all.
modules.whenNot: exactly one choice is wanted (`Klar.Radio`) or the list is long and needs a search box (`Klar.MultiSelect`).

modules.name: Klar.Radio
modules.purpose: A group of radio buttons: choose exactly one of a few options.
modules.whenToUse: two to five options where exactly one is chosen and people should see them all.
modules.whenNot: there are more options (`Klar.Select`), a one-line switch between views is wanted (`Klar.SegmentedControl`) or several may be chosen (`Klar.CheckboxGroup`).

modules.name: Klar.Switch
modules.purpose: An on/off switch for a setting that takes effect at once ("Email notifications").
modules.whenToUse: an on/off setting that takes effect at once, such as email notifications.
modules.whenNot: the choice is part of a form that is saved with a button (`Klar.Checkbox`).

modules.name: Klar.Slider
modules.purpose: A slider for a number in a range, and a range slider with two thumbs.
modules.whenToUse: a number in a known range that is dragged rather than typed, or a range with two thumbs.
modules.whenNot: the number is typed (`Klar.NumberInput`).

modules.name: Klar.SegmentedControl
modules.purpose: A row of joined options where exactly one is chosen: a switch between views ("List" / "Grid"), periods ("Day" / "Week" / "Month") or modes.
modules.whenToUse: a few short options that switch what the page shows, such as List or Grid, or Day, Week and Month.
modules.whenNot: the options need a sentence of explanation (`Klar.Radio`), there are many (`Klar.Select`) or panels of content are switched (`Klar.Tabs`).

modules.name: Klar.MaskedInput
modules.purpose: A field for an identifier that has a fixed shape and, often, a check digit: an IBAN, an organisation number, a bank account, a postal code, a phone number, or a code of your own such as `AB-1234`.
modules.whenToUse: an identifier with a fixed shape and often a check digit, such as an IBAN, an organisation number or a postal code.
modules.whenNot: the text is free (`Klar.TextInput`) or the value is an amount of money (`Klar.MoneyInput`).

modules.name: Klar.Money
modules.purpose: An exact amount of money: a whole number of minor units (øre, cents, yen) together with its currency.
modules.whenToUse: every amount of money the application keeps, adds or splits, in an exact currency.
modules.whenNot: the user types the amount (`Klar.MoneyInput`) or the number is not money, such as a quantity or a percentage (`Klar.NumberInput`).

modules.name: Klar.MoneyInput
modules.purpose: A field for an amount of money in one currency.
modules.whenToUse: the user types an amount of money in one currency and the application needs it as an exact `Klar.Money`.
modules.whenNot: the number is not money (`Klar.NumberInput`) or an amount is only shown (`Klar.Money`).

modules.name: Klar.Select
modules.purpose: A single select with a search box, for lists from a handful to many thousands of options.
modules.whenToUse: exactly one value is chosen from a list of a handful to many thousands of options, and only listed values are valid.
modules.whenNot: the user may type anything (`Klar.Autocomplete`) or several values are chosen (`Klar.MultiSelect`).

modules.name: Klar.Select.Option
modules.purpose: The option model shared by Klar.Select, Klar.MultiSelect and Klar.Autocomplete.
modules.whenToUse: options for a select are built in a module that has no select of its own, such as a data module or a simulated backend.
modules.whenNot: the options are built next to the select itself; `Klar.Select` re-exports the same functions.

modules.name: Klar.Ids
modules.purpose: How the application's own id type is written as text and read back, once.
modules.whenToUse: the application's own id type must be written as text and read back for components that keep text keys.
modules.whenNot: the id is already a `String`; no `Ids` is needed.

modules.name: Klar.MultiSelect
modules.purpose: Choose several values from a searchable list.
modules.whenToUse: several values are chosen from a searchable list, shown as chips in the field.
modules.whenNot: exactly one value is wanted (`Klar.Select`) or a handful of options fit on screen (`Klar.CheckboxGroup`).

modules.name: Klar.Autocomplete
modules.purpose: A text field with suggestions.
modules.whenToUse: free text that often repeats earlier values, such as a city or a company name, where the suggestions only help.
modules.whenNot: only listed values are valid (`Klar.Select`).

modules.name: Klar.VirtualList
modules.purpose: A list of thousands of rows that draws only the rows in view, and is a list box for the keyboard.
modules.whenToUse: a long, plain list of equal rows that people scan and pick from, such as a search result or 50 000 products.
modules.whenNot: the records have columns to sort, filter and compare (`Klar.Table` with `virtual`) or the list is short (`Klar.ListItem`).

modules.name: Klar.Picking
modules.purpose: The vocabulary that Klar.TreeSelect, Klar.Cascader and Klar.Transfer share.
modules.whenToUse: you build the nodes for `Klar.TreeSelect`, `Klar.Cascader` or `Klar.Transfer`, or need one way to write your ids as keys.
modules.whenNot: you show a hierarchy on the page itself with open and closed branches (as `Klar.Tree`, which has its own nodes).

modules.name: Klar.TreeSelect
modules.purpose: A field that opens a popup with a tree and lets the user choose one node, or several with check boxes.
modules.whenToUse: the user picks from a hierarchy that is too big for a plain list (regions and warehouses, product categories, an organisation).
modules.whenNot: the list is short and flat (as `Klar.Select` or `Klar.MultiSelect`), the user drills down through levels (as `Klar.Cascader`) or the tree is shown on the page itself (as `Klar.Tree`).

modules.name: Klar.Cascader
modules.purpose: A field for choosing a path through levels: Region, Country, City; Category, Subcategory, Product.
modules.whenToUse: the user picks one value by drilling down through levels they know, such as country, region and city.
modules.whenNot: the user picks from a tree with check boxes (as `Klar.TreeSelect`) or from one flat list (as `Klar.Select`).

modules.name: Klar.Transfer
modules.purpose: Two lists side by side, "Available" and "Chosen", and a way to move items from one to the other.
modules.whenToUse: the user assigns many things to one thing, such as products to a promotion, users to a group or columns to an export.
modules.whenNot: the user picks a few values from a list (as `Klar.MultiSelect`) or values in a hierarchy (as `Klar.TreeSelect`).

modules.name: Klar.Date
modules.purpose: Calendar dates without a time or a time zone: a year, a month and a day.
modules.whenToUse: the application holds a due date, a delivery date or a birthday, a day that is not a moment in time.
modules.whenNot: you mean an exact moment (use `Time.Posix` from `elm/time`).

modules.name: Klar.DatePicker
modules.purpose: A date field: type the date or pick it in a calendar.
modules.whenToUse: the user enters one date in a form (a due date, a delivery date).
modules.whenNot: the user chooses a period (as `Klar.DateRangePicker`), a date with a time of day (as `Klar.DateTimePicker`) or the calendar should always be visible (as `Klar.Calendar`).

modules.name: Klar.DateRangePicker
modules.purpose: A period field: a from date and a to date in one control, with one calendar that shows two months and a list of quick choices.
modules.whenToUse: the user chooses a period, as in reports, filters and bookings.
modules.whenNot: the user enters a single date (as `Klar.DatePicker`).

modules.name: Klar.TimePicker
modules.purpose: A 24-hour time field: type `14:30` or pick a time from a list.
modules.whenToUse: the user enters a time of day only, such as an order cut-off.
modules.whenNot: the user enters a date and a time together (as `Klar.DateTimePicker`).

modules.name: Klar.DateTimePicker
modules.purpose: A date and a time in one control: a Klar.DatePicker and a Klar.TimePicker side by side under one label.
modules.whenToUse: the date and the time belong together, such as the moment of a pick-up.
modules.whenNot: you need a date alone (as `Klar.DatePicker`) or a time alone (as `Klar.TimePicker`).

modules.name: Klar.Calendar
modules.purpose: A month calendar for choosing a day or a period, with small marks on days.
modules.whenToUse: the calendar should always be visible, such as a delivery schedule or a day chooser beside a list of orders.
modules.whenNot: you need a form field with a popup (as `Klar.DatePicker` or `Klar.DateRangePicker`).

modules.name: Klar.Recurrence
modules.purpose: A rule for dates that repeat ("every second Tuesday", "the last day of the month, ten times").
modules.whenToUse: the application needs the dates of a repeating schedule, a description of it in words or an RRULE for the backend.
modules.whenNot: a person builds the rule in a form (as `Klar.RecurrencePicker`).

modules.name: Klar.RecurrencePicker
modules.purpose: A form field that builds a repeating Klar.Recurrence rule.
modules.whenToUse: a person sets up something that repeats: a standing order, a delivery schedule, a recurring invoice.
modules.whenNot: you need a single date (as `Klar.DatePicker`) or the dates of a rule without a form (as `Klar.Recurrence`).

modules.name: Klar.Table
modules.purpose: A data table for records: search, column filters, sorting, selection with bulk actions, row actions, expandable rows, CSV export and pagination.
modules.whenToUse: people have to find, compare and act on many rows of the same kind: orders, customers, shipments.
modules.whenNot: you show a short list of things to open (as `Klar.ListItem`) or a long, plain list of equal rows (as `Klar.VirtualList`).

modules.name: Klar.Pagination
modules.purpose: Page navigation for long lists and tables: the range shown ("1–25 of 3,000"), rows per page, first / previous / page numbers with ellipsis / next / last, and "Go to page".
modules.whenToUse: you page a list that you fetch or show yourself, outside `Klar.Table`.
modules.whenNot: the list is a `Klar.Table`, which has its own page controls.

modules.name: Klar.ListItem
modules.purpose: A dense list row, and the list that holds the rows.
modules.whenToUse: the application shows records such as orders, tickets and files, a menu of things to open, or a master list next to a detail pane.
modules.whenNot: people must search, sort and act on many rows of one kind (as `Klar.Table`).

modules.name: Klar.Tree
modules.purpose: A tree view for hierarchies: regions and warehouses, folders, product categories, code lists.
modules.whenToUse: a hierarchy is shown on the page itself, with open and closed branches.
modules.whenNot: the user picks a node in a form field (as `Klar.TreeSelect`).

modules.name: Klar.Overlay
modules.purpose: The layer above the page: dialogs, drawers, the command palette, the shortcut sheet and the toasts.
modules.whenToUse: you put dialogs, drawers, toasts or the command palette on the page (one `host` for all of them).
modules.whenNot: you need a menu or a tooltip next to an element (as `Klar.Menu` or `Klar.Tooltip`).

modules.name: Klar.Modal
modules.purpose: A dialog on top of the page, for work that needs the user's full attention: editing a record, a form with several fields, a step of a wizard.
modules.whenToUse: the user must finish a task, such as editing a record or a form with several fields, before doing anything else.
modules.whenNot: a yes-or-no question (use `Klar.ConfirmDialog`), a panel beside the page (use `Klar.Drawer`) or a small panel next to a button (use `Klar.Popover`) is enough.

modules.name: Klar.ConfirmDialog
modules.purpose: The "are you sure?" dialog, with the whole life of the request it guards.
modules.whenToUse: the user must confirm an action that is hard to undo or that affects others, such as deleting an order or canceling a shipment.
modules.whenNot: the dialog is a form with several fields to fill in (use `Klar.Modal`); one or two controls in `body`, such as a reason or a target to choose, are fine.

modules.name: Klar.Drawer
modules.purpose: A panel that slides in from the side of the window: the details of a row in a list, a form with many filters, anything the user wants to see next to the page they came from.
modules.whenToUse: the user looks at details or a form next to the page they came from, such as the details of a row in a list.
modules.whenNot: the task must be finished first (use `Klar.Modal`), the question is yes-or-no (use `Klar.ConfirmDialog`) or the panel is small and next to a button (use `Klar.Popover`).

modules.name: Klar.Toast
modules.purpose: Short notifications that appear in a corner of the window, stack up and go away by themselves: "Order saved", "Could not send the invoice".
modules.whenToUse: the user needs feedback about something they just did, which needs no decision.
modules.whenNot: a message must stay on the page (use `Klar.Alert`) or the user must answer a question (use `Klar.ConfirmDialog`).

modules.name: Klar.Popover
modules.purpose: A small panel anchored to a button, with any content: a quick filter, a few settings, a short form, an explanation with a link.
modules.whenToUse: a small panel next to a button must hold any content, such as a quick filter or a few settings, and stay open while the user works in it.
modules.whenNot: you only need a list of actions (use `Klar.Menu`) or the work needs the full attention of the user (use `Klar.Modal`).

modules.name: Klar.Tooltip
modules.purpose: Short hints that appear when the pointer rests on an element or the keyboard focuses it.
modules.whenToUse: an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut or an unavailable control needs a short hint on hover or focus.
modules.whenNot: the user needs the information to proceed (put it in the page, or use `Klar.Popover` for richer content).

modules.name: Klar.ContextMenu
modules.purpose: The menu that opens where the user right-clicks.
modules.whenToUse: one menu must open where the user right-clicks and serve many elements, such as the rows of a table.
modules.whenNot: the menu opens from a button (use `Klar.Menu`).

modules.name: Klar.CommandPalette
modules.purpose: A command palette: one search box, usually opened with `Ctrl K`, for commands ("New order", "Go to invoices") and for content ("Ada Lovelace").
modules.whenToUse: the application needs one search box for its commands and places, usually opened with Ctrl K.
modules.whenNot: the user chooses one value in a form (use `Klar.Select`) or searches inside a page (use `Klar.SearchInput`).

modules.name: Klar.ShortcutHelp
modules.purpose: The cheat sheet of keyboard shortcuts: a dialog that lists every shortcut of the application, grouped, with key caps and a small filter box.
modules.whenToUse: the user needs a cheat sheet of the keyboard shortcuts the application listens to.
modules.whenNot: you only need to show one shortcut next to a control (use `Klar.Tooltip`).

modules.name: Klar.AppShell
modules.purpose: The frame of a whole application: a top bar, a sidebar and a content area that scrolls on its own.
modules.whenToUse: the application needs a frame with a top bar, a sidebar and a content area, as the root of a `Browser.application` view.
modules.whenNot: you only need a single page without navigation chrome (build it from `Klar.Layout` and `Klar.PageHeader`).

modules.name: Klar.SideNav
modules.purpose: Vertical navigation for the sidebar of an application: sections, links with icons and counts, and groups that open and close.
modules.whenToUse: the sidebar needs vertical navigation with sections, links, counts and groups that open and close.
modules.whenNot: you need tabs inside a page (use `Klar.Tabs`) or the path to the current page (use `Klar.Breadcrumbs`).

modules.name: Klar.PageHeader
modules.purpose: The top of a page: the title, a line of explanation, where the page sits in the application, the state of the thing you are looking at, and what you can do with it.
modules.whenToUse: a page needs a title with its subtitle, status, breadcrumbs, actions and tabs at the top.
modules.whenNot: you need the frame of the whole application (use `Klar.AppShell`) or the title of a card or panel (use `Klar.Card`).

modules.name: Klar.Breadcrumbs
modules.purpose: The path to the current page: links separated by chevrons, where the last item is the current page.
modules.whenToUse: the user must see where the current page sits in the application, as a trail of links.
modules.whenNot: you need the main navigation (use `Klar.SideNav`) or sections within one page (use `Klar.Tabs`).

modules.name: Klar.Tabs
modules.purpose: Tabs that switch between views of the same thing: the overview of an order, its history and its files.
modules.whenToUse: the user switches between views of the same thing, such as the overview, history and files of an order.
modules.whenNot: sections should open and close in place (use `Klar.Accordion`) or the user moves through ordered steps (use `Klar.Stepper`).

modules.name: Klar.Stepper
modules.purpose: The steps of a wizard or a checkout flow, laid out horizontally or vertically.
modules.whenToUse: the user needs to see where they are in the steps of a wizard or a checkout flow.
modules.whenNot: you need switchable views of the same thing (use `Klar.Tabs`) or a plain progress measure (use `Klar.Progress`).

modules.name: Klar.Accordion
modules.purpose: Sections that open and close: the details of a record, groups of settings, advanced filters.
modules.whenToUse: sections of content should open and close in place, such as the details of a record or groups of settings.
modules.whenNot: the sections are views the user switches between (use `Klar.Tabs`).

modules.name: Klar.Toolbar
modules.purpose: A horizontal bar of grouped actions: the strip above a table, the actions of an editor, or the bulk actions that appear when rows are selected.
modules.whenToUse: a row of grouped actions is needed above a table or an editor, or for bulk actions on selected rows.
modules.whenNot: you need a single list of actions in a dropdown (use `Klar.Menu`).

modules.name: Klar.DescriptionList
modules.purpose: Label and value pairs for detail views, rendered as a semantic `dl`.
modules.whenToUse: the application shows the facts about one thing, such as an order, a customer or a shipment.
modules.whenNot: there are many things of the same kind to compare or sort, use `Klar.Table`.

modules.name: Klar.Sortable
modules.purpose: A list the user can put in a new order: by dragging an item by its handle, or with the keyboard.
modules.whenToUse: a short list has an order that matters, such as the steps of a pick sequence or the filters of a saved view.
modules.whenNot: the user only chooses which columns of a table to show (use `Table.columnChooser`); a table has no way to reorder its columns.

modules.name: Klar.Splitter
modules.purpose: Two or more panes side by side (or one above the other) that the user can make larger and smaller by moving the separators between them, with the mouse, a finger or the keyboard.
modules.whenToUse: the user should resize a master and its detail, a navigator beside a work area or an editor above a preview.
modules.whenNot: the layout is fixed, use `Klar.Layout`, or when sections only open and close, use `Klar.Accordion`.

modules.name: Klar.StatusPage
modules.purpose: A page that stands for a whole result: "Order created", "No access", "Page not found", "Something went wrong on our side", "Down for maintenance".
modules.whenToUse: the whole page is one result, such as not found, no access, a server error, maintenance or success after a submit.
modules.whenNot: the result sits inside a table, card or panel, use `Klar.EmptyState` or `Klar.ErrorState`.

modules.name: Klar.BulkBar
modules.purpose: The bar of actions for the items the user has selected: "12 selected: Export, Delete".
modules.whenToUse: a list, a grid of cards or another selectable collection needs actions for the selected items.
modules.whenNot: the items are in a `Klar.Table`, which draws a bar of its own for its selection.

modules.name: Klar.LeaveGuard
modules.purpose: Asks "Leave without saving?" when the user leaves a page with unsaved work: by a link, by your own code and by the browser's Back and Forward buttons.
modules.whenToUse: a page holds unsaved work and every way of leaving it, including Back and Forward, must ask first.
modules.whenNot: only the unsaved state itself is needed without a dialog, read it with `isDirty` or compare values in your own model.

modules.name: Klar.History
modules.purpose: Undo and redo for a form or an editor: a value, the values it had before and the values it had before you undid them.
modules.whenToUse: a form or an editor needs undo and redo, or a dirty check against the last saved value.
modules.whenNot: only a "leave without saving" question is needed, use `Klar.LeaveGuard`.

modules.name: Klar.Markdown
modules.purpose: Markdown as safe, calm HTML: for the text of a note, a description, a help page, or the answer of a language model that is still being written.
modules.whenToUse: text written in Markdown, also by someone else or by a model, must be shown as safe HTML.
modules.whenNot: the user is to write the text, use `Klar.MarkdownEditor`.

modules.name: Klar.MarkdownEditor
modules.purpose: A text area for Markdown with a toolbar and a live preview: the editor of a note, a description, a comment, or the instruction to a language model.
modules.whenToUse: the user writes Markdown and should see the result as it is typed.
modules.whenNot: the text is only shown, use `Klar.Markdown`, or when plain text is enough, use `Klar.TextArea`.

modules.name: Klar.Diff
modules.purpose: What changed between two versions of a text, of a JSON document or of a record, shown so that a person can see it and decide.
modules.whenToUse: a person must see what changed between two versions of a text, a JSON value or a record, such as in a review or an audit log.
modules.whenNot: several records are shown side by side, use `Klar.Compare`, or when there is only one JSON value, use `Klar.JsonViewer`.

modules.name: Klar.Compare
modules.purpose: Records side by side, with the differences marked: two or more products, two versions of an order, "your version" against "theirs".
modules.whenToUse: two or more records are read side by side and the application wants to see where they differ.
modules.whenNot: the change between two versions of one text or record is the point, use `Klar.Diff`.

modules.name: Klar.PermissionMatrix
modules.purpose: A grid of roles and permissions that says what each role may do, and lets an administrator change it: the classic screen of an application with users.
modules.whenToUse: an administrator sets which roles may do what, in a grid of roles and permissions.
modules.whenNot: only a list of options is chosen for one user, use `Klar.CheckboxGroup`.

modules.name: Klar.ApprovalFlow
modules.purpose: The approval process of one item: an ordered list of steps, each with one or several approvers and a decision from each, and where the item stands.
modules.whenToUse: an invoice, a credit note or a request needs sign-off and the page shows who has decided and who is next.
modules.whenNot: only a history of what happened is shown, use `Klar.Timeline`, or the steps of a wizard, use `Klar.Stepper`.

modules.name: Klar.Stat
modules.purpose: A KPI tile: one number with its label, the change since last time, a short note and optionally a trend line.
modules.whenToUse: a headline number is read at a glance on a dashboard or at the top of a page.
modules.whenNot: there are several label and value pairs, use `Klar.DescriptionList`, or one value against a scale, use `gauge` or `meter` from `Klar.Chart`.

modules.name: Klar.Chart
modules.purpose: Line, bar, donut, gauge, meter and sparkline charts, drawn without any chart or SVG package.
modules.whenToUse: numbers are shown as a trend, a comparison of categories, parts of a whole or one value against a scale.
modules.whenNot: the progress of a task is shown, use `Klar.Progress`.

modules.name: Klar.Timeline
modules.purpose: A vertical history of events: an audit trail, an order log, an activity feed.
modules.whenToUse: a history of events is shown newest first, grouped by day, such as an audit trail or an order log.
modules.whenNot: the events are rules and decisions of an approval process, use `Klar.ApprovalFlow`.

modules.name: Klar.Avatar
modules.purpose: Avatars: a person, an organization or a system shown as a small badge with initials, a picture or an icon.
modules.whenToUse: a person, an organization or a system is shown as a small badge with initials, a picture or an icon.
modules.whenNot: a short text label or status is shown, use `Klar.Badge`.

modules.name: Klar.JsonViewer
modules.purpose: A collapsible tree for looking at JSON: an API response, a stored document, a request body.
modules.whenToUse: the application shows a JSON value, such as an API response or a stored document, that the user needs to explore.
modules.whenNot: a short snippet is enough (`codeBlock` of `Klar.Text`).

modules.name: Klar.Rule
modules.purpose: Rules as plain data: a tree of conditions and groups that you can edit, check, run against your rows, describe in words and store as JSON.
modules.whenToUse: filter conditions are data that the application stores, runs against its rows or describes in words.
modules.whenNot: the user must edit the conditions (use `Klar.RuleBuilder` or `Klar.FilterBar`).

modules.name: Klar.RuleBuilder
modules.purpose: A visual editor for rules: groups of conditions that the user builds, rearranges and reads as a sentence, drawn with thin gray connector lines.
modules.whenToUse: users need the full power of nested "all of" and "any of" groups of conditions.
modules.whenNot: a row of filter chips above a table is enough (use `Klar.FilterBar`).

modules.name: Klar.FilterBar
modules.purpose: Quick filters above a table: the conditions that are on, shown as chips ("Status is Paid"), an "Add filter" button that opens a small editor (field, operator, value), and optional preset pills like ...
modules.whenToUse: users filter a table with a few quick conditions shown as chips and presets.
modules.whenNot: users need nested groups of conditions (use `Klar.RuleBuilder`).

modules.name: Klar.SavedViews
modules.purpose: Named, saved filters ("views"): a dropdown button that lists the saved views and lets the user apply one, save the current filter under a new name, rename and delete views (after an inline ...
modules.whenToUse: users want to save, name and reapply their filters.
modules.whenNot: the filter is fixed and has no names to remember (use `Klar.FilterBar` alone).

modules.name: Klar.ServerList
modules.purpose: A list whose rows live on a server: a table, a filter bar and saved views that edit one query, and the glue that every such list needs, in one place.
modules.whenToUse: a screen is a table of rows that the server searches, filters, sorts and pages, with a filter bar and saved views.
modules.whenNot: you have all the rows (use `Klar.Table` in client mode) or only one of the parts (use `Klar.Table` with `server`).

modules.name: Klar.Remote
modules.purpose: The state of data that comes from a backend: not asked for yet, loading, failed, or here.
modules.whenToUse: a screen shows data that comes from a backend and can be loading, failed or old.
modules.whenNot: the data is always there, as a plain value in the model.

modules.name: Klar.RemoteView
modules.purpose: The body of a card, a dialog or a drawer that shows one piece of remote data: a loading skeleton that screen readers hear, the failure with a retry, and the data, old or being refreshed.
modules.whenToUse: the body of a card, a dialog or a drawer shows one piece of remote data.
modules.whenNot: the data is a table or a list (use `Klar.Table` or `Klar.ListItem`, which take a `Remote` themselves).

modules.name: Klar.Search
modules.purpose: Text matching for search fields, selects and command palettes: forgiving about case and accents, and ranked, so the best match comes first.
modules.whenToUse: a search field, a select or a list needs forgiving, ranked text matching.
modules.whenNot: the match must be exact, such as an id (compare the strings yourself).

modules.name: Klar.Format
modules.purpose: Formatting numbers, sizes, dates and times for people, in the conventions of a `Locale`.
modules.whenToUse: the application shows numbers, sizes, dates or times to people.
modules.whenNot: the text is a machine format (use `iso8601` for a date in data, or the plain value).

modules.name: Klar.Shortcut
modules.purpose: Global keyboard shortcuts for the whole application, including sequences of two keys such as `g` then `m`.
modules.whenToUse: the application needs global keyboard shortcuts, including sequences of two keys.
modules.whenNot: a key only matters inside one component (use that component's own key handling).

modules.name: Klar.Icon.Library
modules.purpose: The whole icon library in one place, for galleries, pickers and tests.
modules.whenToUse: you need a gallery, a picker or a test that goes through every icon.
modules.whenNot: the application only shows some icons (import them from their modules, or `Klar.Icon` for the everyday set).
